guahanu: gwahanu (gwahanu) — to part, separate; verbal noun, fronted before a wnaethont (A guahanu a wnaethont 'and they parted'); no mutation
wnaethont: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 pl. preterite 'they did', soft-mutated after a (the 'verbal noun + a wnaethont' auxiliary construction: Bwyta a chyuedach a wnaethont 'they ate and feasted')
chwedleu: chwedl (chwedl) — tale, story, talk; noun f., plural chwedleu (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); ch- does not mutate here
ereill: arall (arall) — other; plural ereill, the plural form of the adjective (y chwedleu ereill 'the other tales'); modern eraill
trossei: trosi (trosi) — to turn, turn over; 3 sg. imperfect 'he would turn' (y chwedleu ereill y trossei ynteu 'he would turn to other tales'); no mutation after the particle y
odyna: odyna (oddyna) — thence, then, after that; adverb, o 'from' + dyna 'there' (Odyna treulaw y ulwydyn 'then the year was spent')
ganuet: canuet (canfed) — hundredth; ordinal, soft-mutated after possessive y/dy 'his/your' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen', literally 'on his hundredth horseman'; the idiom means a company of a hundred riders)
marchauc: marchawc (marchog) — horseman, rider; noun m., spelt -auc (ar y ganuet marchauc); base form
ryngtaw: rwng (rhwng) + ef — 'between him'; conjugated preposition, 3 sg. m., used in the idiom ryngtaw a 'between him and' = on his way to (Ef a aeth ryngtaw a llys Eueyd Hen 'he went his way to the court of Heueyd the Old')
eueyd: Heueyd (Hefeydd) — proper name, Rhiannon's father; spelt Eueyd without the h- (Eueyd Hen 'Heueyd the Old')
uuwyt: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'there was' (llawen uuwyt wrthaw 'he was welcomed gladly', literally 'glad it was to him'), soft-mutated (b>u) after the fronted predicate llawen
llewenyd: llewenyd (llawenydd) — joy, gladness; noun m. (dygyuor a llewenyd 'a gathering and gladness')
arlwy: arlwy (arlwy) — provision, banquet, preparation of food; noun m. (arlwy mawr 'a great banquet'; y wled a'r arlwy 'the feast and the fare')
uaranned: baraned (obsolete) — provisions, supplies, stores; noun pl. (holl uaranned y llys 'all the provisions of the court'); soft-mutated after holl 'all'; the word is rare and its sense is taken from the context
gynghor: kynghor (cyngor) — counsel, advice, will; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (wrth y gynghor ef 'by his counsel'; gan gynghor 'by the counsel of')
treulwyt: treulaw (treulio) — to spend, pass (time or goods); 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was spent' (holl uaranned y llys … y treulwyt 'all the court's provisions were spent'); no mutation after the particle y
kyweiryaw: kyweiraw (cyweirio) — to set in order, make ready; verbal noun, spelt -yaw, fronted before a wnaethpwyt (Kyweiryaw y neuad a wnaethpwyt 'the hall was made ready')
wnaethpwyt: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 3 sg. impersonal preterite 'was done', soft-mutated after a (a wnaethpwyt 'was done'), -pwyt as the impersonal ending
eistedyssont: eisted (eistedd) — to sit; 3 pl. pluperfect 'they had sat', here with past sense (ual yd eistedyssont 'how they sat'); -yssont the ending; ss for s
enryded: anryded (anrhydedd) — honour, rank, dignity; noun f., spelt enryded (ual y bei y enryded 'according to his rank'); y 'his' gives no change before a vowel
kyuedach: kyuedach (cyfeddach) — carousing, a drinking-feast; noun m., base form (ar dechreu kyuedach 'at the start of the carousing')
gwineu: gwineu (gwinau) — dark brown, dark-haired; adjective (guas gwineu 'a dark-haired lad'); after a masculine noun, no mutation
teyrneid: teyrneid (teyrnaidd) — kingly, princely, lordly; adjective, from teyrn 'king' + -eid (guas … teyrneid 'a lad of lordly bearing')
guisc: gwisc (gwisg) — garment, dress; noun, spelt gu for gw (a guisc o bali 'and a garment of brocade'); g- is not changed by a 'and'
gynted: kynted (cyntedd) — porch, entrance, fore-part; noun m., soft-mutated after y 'to' (y gynted y neuad 'to the porch of the hall'); the sense 'entrance' is that of GPC cyntedd, and fits the context
gedymdeithon: kedymdeith (cydymaith) — companion; plural -on, soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (a'y gedymdeithon 'and his companions')
cressaw: croesaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m., spelt cressaw (Cressaw Duw wrthyt 'God's welcome to you')
eneit: eneit (enaid) — soul; used in address as an endearment 'dear one, my soul' (a dos y eisted, eneit 'and go to sit, friend')
eirchat: eirchat (eirchiad) — suppliant, petitioner, one who asks a boon; noun m. (eirchat wyf 'I am a petitioner')
erchi: erchi (erchi) — to ask, request, bid; verbal noun (y erchi it 'to ask of you')
dodwyf: dyuot (dod) — to come; 1 sg. 'I am come, I have come', built on the stem dod- with wyf (y erchi it y dodwyf 'it is to ask you that I have come'); y the relative/particle after a fronted phrase
arch: arch (arch) — (1) request, boon, petition; noun f. (beth yw dy arch di 'what is your request'); (2) 2 sg. imperative of erchi 'ask!' (nac arch dim 'ask nothing')
erchych: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 2 sg. present subjunctive 'you may ask' (Pa arch bynnac a erchych di ymi 'whatever request you may ask of me'); e- no change after relative a
gaffael: caffael (cael) — to get, obtain; verbal noun, soft-mutated after y 'it/its' (hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it')
itti: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition (y 'to' + ti), spelt itti (itti y byd 'you shall have it')
och: och (och) — alas; interjection of dismay (Och! heb y Riannon 'Alas, said Rhiannon')
rody: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 2 sg. present 'you give' (paham y rody di attep y uelly 'why do you give an answer so?'); no mutation after the particle y
uelly: melly (felly) — thus, so, in that way; adverb, soft-mutated (m>u) in the phrase y uelly 'in such a way', the y being a particle of manner (attep y uelly 'an answer so'; ac y uelly guare 'and so they played')
neus: neu + 's — the affirmative particle neu 'indeed' with infixed 3 sg. object pronoun 's 'it' (Neus rodes y uelly 'you have indeed given it so')
yg: yn (yn) — in; preposition, spelt yg before a g: the g is the written trace of the nasal mutation (yg gwyd = yng ngwyd 'in the presence of'; yg got = yng nghod 'in a bag', with c>ngh after yn 'in')
gwyd: gwyd (gŵydd) — presence, sight; noun m., in the phrase yg gwyd 'in the presence of' (yg gwyd gwyrda 'in the presence of noblemen'), with the nasal mutation after yn written yg gwyd
garaf: caru (caru) — to love; 1 sg. present 'I love', soft-mutated after relative a (y wreic uwyaf a garaf 'the woman I love most')
kyscu: kyscu (cysgu) — to sleep; verbal noun, base form (yd wyt yn kyscu heno 'you are to sleep tonight')
herchi: erchi (erchi) — to ask; verbal noun, with h-prefix after y 'her' (y herchi hi 'to ask her')
darmerth: darmerth (obsolete) — provision, entertainment, banquet; noun, rare word paired with arlwy and wled (y wled a'r arlwy a'r darmerth); the meaning is taken from the context and is not certain
ymma: ymma (yma) — here; adverb, spelling with mm (yssyd ymma 'is here')
kynhewi: kynhewi (obsolete) — to fall silent, hold one's peace; verbal noun, fronted before a oruc (Kynhewi a oruc Pwyll 'Pwyll fell silent'); the sense is that of the context
rodassei: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had given' (attep a rodassei 'the answer he had given')
taw: tewi (tewi) — to be silent; 2 sg. imperative 'be silent!, hush' (Taw, hyt y mynnych 'be quiet, as much as you like'); modern taw
uuscrellach: buscrell (obsolete) — foolish, stupid; the comparative in -ach, 'more foolish', soft-mutated (b>u) as the predicate after ny bu (ny bu uuscrellach gwr 'no man was more foolish')
ssynnwyr: synnwyr (synnwyr) — sense, understanding, wits; noun m., spelt ss (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses')
nog: noc (nag) — than; comparative conjunction, spelt nog before ry (nog ry uuost ti 'than you have been')
uuost: bot (bod) — to be; 2 sg. preterite 'you were, you have been', soft-mutated after the perfective particle ry (ry uuost ti)
mynyssit: mynnu (mynnu) — to wish, intend; impersonal pluperfect 'it had been intended' (y gwr y mynyssit uy rodi i idaw 'the man to whom it had been intended to give me'), with y the oblique relative
hanuod: anuod (anfodd) — displeasure, unwillingness; noun m., with h-prefix after the contracted 'm 'my' (o'm hanuod 'against my will')
guawl: Gwawl — proper name (Gwawl uab Clut), also gwawl 'light, radiance' as a common word; spelt guawl, no mutation as the subject (Guawl uab Clut)
uab: mab (mab) — son; noun m., soft-mutated after a personal name in a patronymic (Guawl uab Clut 'Gwawl son of Clud')
clut: Clud (Clud) — proper name, the father of Gwawl (Gwawl uab Clut); the name is spelt Clut
tormynnawc: tormynnawc (obsolete) — meaning uncertain, perhaps 'turbulent, domineering, overbearing' (from tormyn 'tumult'); adjective after gwr, paired with kyuoethawc 'mighty' (gwr tormynnawc, kyuoethawc); a disputed reading
kyuoethawc: kyuoethawc (cyfoethog) — wealthy, mighty, rich in dominion; adjective, from kyuoeth 'realm, wealth' + -awc (gwr … kyuoethawc 'a mighty man')
chan: can (can) — since, because; conjunction, spirant-mutated after a 'and' (A chan derw yt dywedut 'and since it is true that you said')
derw: derw (obsolete) — true, certain, right; adjective (a chan derw yt dywedut y geir a dywedeist 'and since it is certain that you spoke the word you spoke'); the exact construction is not clear
yt: itt (iti) — to you; 2 sg. conjugated preposition, spelt yt (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good'; rac anglot yt 'lest dishonour (come) to you'; ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'); in derw yt dywedut the construction is uncertain, possibly the same 'for you'
dywedeist: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. preterite 'you said' (y geir a dywedeist 'the word you said'), modern dywedaist
rac: rac (rhag) — before, lest, to prevent, for fear of; preposition (dyro ui idaw rac anglot yt 'give me to him to spare you dishonour')
allaf: gallu (gallu) — to be able; 1 sg. present 'I can', with g lost by soft mutation after ny (Ny allaf ui … 'I cannot')
uyth: byth (byth) — ever; with a negative, 'never'; adverb, soft-mutated (b>u) when used adverbially after the verb (dywedy di uyth 'you ever say'; na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'that he may never get me'; a uyd llawn dy got uyth 'will your bag ever be full')
chaffo: caffael (cael) — to get; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may get', spirant-mutated (c>ch) after na 'that … not' (na chaffo ef uiui 'that he may not get me')
got: cot (cod) — bag, pouch, sack; noun f., soft-mutated (c>g): after the article y/'r (y got, a'r got), after possessive dy (dy got), and as a feminine noun after the verb rodaf 'I give' as its object (got uechan 'a small bag')
uechan: bychan (bychan) — small; adjective, soft-mutated (b>u) after a feminine noun (got uechan 'a small bag'); modern bychan, bach
eirch: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 3 sg. present 'asks, will ask' (ef a eirch y wled 'he will ask for the feast'), with ei for e in the 3 sg. present
wled: gwled (gwledd) — feast, banquet; noun f., soft-mutated after the article y as a feminine noun (y wled 'the feast'; y wled honno 'that feast')
niueroed: niuer (nifer) — company, host, number; noun m., plural niueroed (y wled y'r teulu a'r niueroed 'the feast to the household and the hosts')
amdanaf: am — conjugated preposition 'about me'; Amdanaf innheu 'as for me, for my part' (1 sg.)
genhyt: gan — conjugated preposition 'with you' (2 sg.), a variant spelling of gennyt (a'r got honn genhyt 'and this bag with you')
perllan: perllan (perllan) — orchard; noun f. (yn y perllan 'in the orchard'); base form
uchot: uchod (uchod) — above, up there; adverb, spelt uchot (yn y perllan uchot 'in the orchard above')
uo: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may be', soft-mutated after phan 'when' (phan uo ef ar perued 'when he is in the middle of')
gyuedach: kyuedach (cyfeddach) — carousing; noun m., soft-mutated after possessive y 'his' (a'y gyuedach 'and his carousing')
dyret: dyuot (dod) — to come; 2 sg. imperative 'come!' (dyret titheu dy hun y mywn 'you come in yourself'); the ancestor of modern dere
reudus: reudus (obsolete) — meaning uncertain, perhaps 'ragged, shabby, poor'; adjective after dillat 'clothes' (dillat reudus amdanat 'worn clothes about you'), the sense fitting the disguise of a poor man; disputed
amdanat: am — conjugated preposition 'about you' (2 sg.) (dillat reudus amdanat 'ragged clothes on you')
lloneit: lloneit (llond) — a fill, a full measure, as much as will fill; noun m. (lloneit y got o uwyt 'the bag's full of food'; lloneit y got uechan 'a small bagful')
minheu: minheu (minnau) — I for my part; conjunctive 1 sg. pronoun, beside innheu (Minheu a baraf 'and I for my part will cause')
dottit: dodi (dodi) — to put; impersonal imperfect subjunctive 'were put' (bei dottit yssyd … o uwyt 'were all the food … put (into it)'); tt for t
bydei: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperfect/conditional 'would be' (na bydei launach no chynt 'it would not be fuller than before'); b is not changed after na
launach: llawnach (llawnach) — fuller; comparative of llawn, spelt launach, soft-mutated as the predicate after bydei (na bydei launach 'it would not be fuller')
byryer: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast; impersonal present subjunctive 'be thrown', after guedy (guedy byryer llawer yndi 'after much be cast into it')
llawer: llawer (llawer) — much, many; noun/adverb (guedy byryer llawer yndi 'after much has been thrown into it')
llawn: llawn (llawn) — full; adjective (a uyd llawn dy got ti uyth 'will your bag ever be full?')
dywet: dywedut (dweud) — to say; 2 sg. imperative 'say!' (Dywet titheu 'you say')
ony: ony (oni) — unless, until; conjunction ('no, unless …'), causes spirant mutation of c, p, t (ony chyuyt 'unless there rise')
chyuyt: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may rise' (ony chyuyt dylyedauc 'unless a nobleman rise'), spirant-mutated (k>ch) after ony
chyuoethauc: kyuoethawc (cyfoethog) — mighty, wealthy; adjective, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after tra 'very' (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty')
guascu: gwasgu (gwasgu) — to press, tread down; verbal noun (a guascu a'y deudroet y bwyt 'and tread the food down with his two feet'); g not changed by a 'and'
deudroet: deudroed (deudroed) — two feet; deu 'two' + troed, the t softened (d) after deu (a'y deudroet 'with his two feet'); modern deudroed
digawn: digawn (digon) — enough, sufficient; adjective/noun (Digawn ry dodet ymman 'enough has been put here'; digawn yw hynny 'that is enough')
dodet: dodi (dodi) — to put; impersonal 'has been put', after the perfective particle ry (ry dodet ymman 'has been put here')
ymman: ymma (yma) — here; adverb, spelt ymman, with a final n (ry dodet ymman 'put here')
sseghi: senghi (sengi) — to tread, trample; verbal noun, a slip or variant for ssenghi with the n dropped (y sseghi y bwyt yn y got 'to trample the food in the bag'), after y 'to'
el: mynet (mynd) — to go; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may go' (A phan el ef 'when he goes'; yny el ef dros y pen 'until he goes over the head')
tro: troi (troi) — to turn; 2 sg. imperative 'turn!' (tro ditheu y got 'you turn the bag')
glwm: clwm (cwlwm) — knot; noun m., soft-mutated (c>g) as the object of the verbal noun llad 'to tie' (llad glwm 'to tie a knot')
garryeu: carrai (carrai) — strap, thong; noun, plural carryeu, soft-mutated (c>g) after ar 'on' (ar garryeu y got 'on the straps of the bag')
bit: bot (bod) — to be; 3 sg. imperative 'let there be, let it be' (A bit corn canu da 'and let there be a good horn for blowing'; bit hynny yn arwyd 'let that be the signal'); modern bydded
corn: corn (corn) — horn; noun m. (corn canu 'a horn for blowing')
rwymedic: rwymedic (rhwymedig) — bound, tied; past participle in -edic of rwymo 'to bind' (yn rwymedic yn y got 'bound in the bag')
dot: dodi (dodi) — to put; 2 sg. imperative 'put!' (dot titheu lef ar dy gorn 'give a blast on your horn', literally 'put a cry')
lef: llef (llef) — cry, shout, blast; noun f., spelt lef, soft-mutated as the object of dot 'put' (dot lef 'give a cry')
arwyd: arwyd (arwydd) — sign, signal; noun m. (bit hynny yn arwyd 'let that be the signal')
rot: rhawd (obsolete here) — probably 'company, host, troop'; noun, in y rot a'th uarchogyon 'the company and your horsemen'; the reading is uncertain (compare rhawd 'course, band')
uarchogyon: marchawc (marchog) — horseman, rider; plural marchogyon, soft-mutated after possessive 'th 'your' (a'th uarchogyon 'and your horsemen')
glywhont: clywet (clywed) — to hear; 3 pl. present subjunctive 'they may hear', soft-mutated (c>g) after pan 'when' (pan glywhont llef dy gorn 'when they hear the blast of your horn')
diskynnent: disgyn (disgyn) — to descend, come down; 3 pl. imperative 'let them come down' (diskynnent wynteu am pen y llys 'let them come down about the head of the court')
madws: madws (obsolete) — meaning disputed; here probably 'preferable, more fitting' (madws oed ymi cael attep 'it would be better for me to get an answer'); predicative adjective with oed
ercheis: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 1 sg. preterite 'I asked' (am a ercheis 'for what I asked'), modern erchais
kymeint: kymeint (cymaint) — as much, so much, as great; noun/pronoun, kymeint ac 'as much as' (Kymeint ac a ercheist 'as much as you asked')
ercheist: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 2 sg. preterite 'you asked' (a ercheist 'that you asked'), modern erchaist
medyant: medyant (meddiant) — possession, power; noun m., base form (y'm medyant i 'in my possession')
darpar: darpar (darpar) — preparation, provision; noun m. (y wled a'r darpar 'the feast and the preparation')
rodeis: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 1 sg. preterite 'I gave' (hwnnw a rodeis i 'that I gave')
eidawaf: eidaw (obsolete) — meaning uncertain; 1 sg. present, probably 'I allow, I grant' or 'I own (the right)' (nit eidawaf y rodi y neb 'I will not allow it to be given to anyone')
gwawl: Gwawl — proper name; also gwawl 'light'; subject of a verb, no mutation (Gwawl a gerdawd 'Gwawl went')
gerdawd: kerdet (cerdded) — to walk, travel, go; 3 sg. preterite 'went', soft-mutated (c>g) after a (Gwawl a gerdawd ryngthaw a'y gyuoeth 'Gwawl went his way to his realm')
ryngthaw: rwng (rhwng) + ef — 'between him'; 3 sg. m. conjugated preposition, spelt with th (ryngthaw a'y gyuoeth 'on his way to his realm')
gwaul: Gwawl — proper name, a variant spelling Gwaul (Gwaul uab Clut)
annwn: Annwn (Annwn) — the otherworld; proper name, in Penn Annwn 'Head of Annwn' (Pwyll Penn Annwn); spelt annwn here, unlike Annwuyn elsewhere
berllan: perllan (perllan) — orchard; noun f., soft-mutated (p>b) after the article as a feminine noun (y'r berllan 'to the orchard')
gorchymynnassei: gorchymyn (gorchymyn) — to command, instruct; 3 sg. pluperfect 'had instructed' (ual y gorchymynnassei Riannon idaw 'as Rhiannon had instructed him')
gwiscaw: gwiscaw (gwisgo) — to put on, wear; verbal noun, fronted before a oruc (Gwiscaw bratteu trwm … a oruc Pwyll 'Pwyll put on heavy rags')
bratteu: brat (brat) — cloak, rag; noun m., plural bratteu, here the beggar's rags (bratteu trwm 'heavy rags')
trwm: trwm (trwm) — heavy; adjective (bratteu trwm 'heavy rags'), no mutation after a plural noun
ymdanw: am — conjugated preposition 'about him' (3 sg. m.), a slip or contraction for ymdanaw with the a omitted; ym- is a spelling variant of am- (gwiscaw bratteu trwm ymdanw 'putting heavy rags about him')
chymryt: kymryt (cymryd) — to take, put on; verbal noun, spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chymryt lloppaneu 'and putting on clouts')
lloppaneu: lloppan (obsolete) — a clout, old shoe, rough footwear; noun, plural lloppaneu (cymryt lloppaneu mawr am y draet 'taking big shoes on his feet'); the meaning is taken from the context and is uncertain
draet: troet (troed) — foot; noun, plural traed, soft-mutated (t>d) after possessive y 'his' (am y draet 'about his feet')
wedy: gwedy (gwedi) — after; preposition, spelt without g, as in modern wedi (wedy bwyta 'after the eating'); the loss of g is a variant spelling, there is no clear softening word
wawl: Gwawl — proper name, g lost by soft mutation after y 'to' (kyuarch guell a wnaeth y Wawl 'greeted Gwawl')
gwraged: gwreic (gwraig) — woman, wife; noun f., plural gwraged (modern gwragedd) (a gwraged 'and women'; gwyr a gwraged 'men and women')
ro: rodi (rhoi) — to give; 3 sg. present subjunctive 'may he give', soft after the optative a (Duw a ro da yt 'may God give you good')
chraessaw: croesaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m., spelt craessaw, spirant-mutated (c>ch) after a 'and' (a chraessaw Duw wrthyt 'and God's welcome to you')
negessawl: negessawl (obsolete) — on an errand, having a message; adjective, from neges 'errand' + -awl (Negessawl wyf wrthyt 'I am on an errand to you')
craessaw: croesaw (croeso) — welcome; noun m., spelt craessaw (Craessaw wrth dy neges 'welcome to your errand')
gyuartal: kyuartal (cyfartal) — equal, fair, even; adjective, soft-mutated (k>g) after the feminine noun arch (arch gyuartal 'a fair request')
erchy: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 2 sg. present 'you ask' (a erchy ymi 'that you ask of me')
kyuartal: kyuartal (cyfartal) — equal, fair; adjective used as a predicate, base form (Kyuartal, Arglwyd 'A fair (request), lord')
archaf: erchi (erchi) — to ask; 1 sg. present 'I ask', spelt with a (a-affection) (nyt archaf 'I do not ask'; Sef arch a archaf 'this is the request I ask')
didraha: didraha (obsolete) — modest, not excessive, easy to grant; adjective, di- 'without' + traha 'excess, arrogance' (Arch didraha yw honno 'that is a modest request'); the sense is from the context
riuedi: riuedi (obsolete) — a great number, multitude; noun (Riuedi mawr o sswydwyr 'a great number of officers')
sswydwyr: swyddwr (swyddog) — officer, attendant; plural swyddwyr, spelt sswydwyr; the modern word is swyddog
gyuodassant: kyuodi (codi) — to rise; 3 pl. pluperfect 'had risen', soft-mutated (k>g) after relative a (a gyuodassant y uynyd 'who rose up')
llenwi: llenwi (llenwi) — to fill; verbal noun (dechreu llenwi y got 'beginning to fill the bag')
uyrit: bwrw (bwrw) — to throw, cast; impersonal imperfect 'was thrown', soft-mutated (b>u) after relative a (yr a uyrit yndi 'however much was thrown into it')
lawnach: llawnach (llawnach) — fuller; comparative of llawn, spelt lawnach (ny bydei lawnach no chynt 'it would not be fuller than before'); ll soft-mutated as the predicate after bydei
dotter: dodi (dodi) — to put; impersonal present subjunctive 'is put' (yr a dotter yndi uyth 'however much is put into it')
tir: tir (tir) — land, territory; noun m. (dylyedauc tir a dayar 'a lord of land and earth')
chyuoeth: kyuoeth (cyfoeth) — realm, wealth; noun m., spirant-mutated (k>ch) after a 'and' (a chyuoeth 'and realm')
ssenghi: senghi (sengi) — to tread, trample; verbal noun, ss for s (a ssenghi a'y deudroet y bwyt 'and tread the food with his two feet')

__broaden__.ulwydyn: blwydyn (blwyddyn) — year; noun f., soft-mutated after y/the feminine article (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn) · also adverbial, 'a year' in time phrases, soft-mutated without the article (ulwydyn y heno 'a year from tonight'; ual yd eistedyssant ulwydyn o'r nos honno 'as they sat a year from that night'), the soft mutation being that of an adverbial accusative of time
__broaden__.hyt: hyt (hyd) — as far as, until; preposition/conjunction (hyt ym penn y ulwydyn 'until the year's end'; hyt na bo 'so that there be not') · also ar hyt 'along' (ar hyt y prifford 'along the highway') · also 'as far as, so far as, as much as, to the extent that' with the subjunctive (hyt y mynnych 'as much as you wish'; hyt y gallwyf y gaffael 'as far as I can get it'); hyt oet y wled 'until the time of the feast'
__broaden__.ar: ar — (1) preposition 'on, upon; at' (ar Hafgan; ar y carw; ar y gilyd 'against the other'); (2) the article yr after a vowel, 'that which' (noc ar a uu 'than what was'; Ar ny del 'and whoever does not come') · also (3) 'with, accompanied by' (ar y ganuet marchauc 'with his hundred horsemen'); 'in' (ar y ssynnwyr e hun 'in his own senses'; ar perued y digrifwch 'in the middle of the merriment'); ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'; ar uyrr 'quickly'; ar hynny 'thereupon' (see yny)
__broaden__.y: y — (1) the article 'the' (y llys); (2) 'his, her, its' (y uryt: soft mutation = his; y hymdidan: h-prefix = her); (3) 'to' (y hela, y gyuoeth); (4) preverbal particle after a fronted adverb or object (yno y bu, Pwyll... a oed); (5) the relative in oblique relations (o'r a welsei) · (6) 'from' in y gan, y wrth 'from, compared with' (y gan y uarch 'from his horse'; y wrth y ffryt hi 'compared with her form'); (7) infixed object 'him, her, it' after a (a'y guelei 'who saw her'); (8) in a'y kymriw it is the second letter of ae 'either' (see a) · also (9) y am, y amdanaw 'from about, off' (y amdanaw 'off him'; y am hynny 'concerning that')
__broaden__.o: o (o) — (1) 'of, from' preposition; (2) 'if' before a verb (o gwneuthum gam 'if I did wrong') · also 'on, by' (o pedestric 'on foot'), 'out of, from' (o'th garyat ti 'from love of you'), 'of' a kind (pryt … o uorwyn 'the looks of (any) maiden') · also agent after a verbal noun, 'by' (troi o Pwyll y got 'Pwyll turning the bag'); o gosp 'of punishment'
__broaden__.law: llaw (llaw) — hand; noun f., soft-mutated after heb in heb law 'past, beside' (heb law yr orssed 'past the mound') · also 'side' in ar neill law 'on one side' (ar neill law Pwyll 'on one side of Pwyll'), soft after neill; 'hand' after possessive 'th (y'th law 'in your hand')
__broaden__.dechreu: dechreu (dechrau) — to begin; verbal noun (dechreu dygyuor 'beginning to muster') · also the noun 'beginning' (ar dechreu kyuedach 'at the start of the carousing')
__broaden__.nac: nac — (1) negative used in a direct answer, repeating the verb, 'no' (Nac attygaf 'I will not'); (2) 'nor' before a vowel (nac ymdidan) · also negative imperative 'do not' (nac arch dim 'do not ask anything')
__broaden__.wnaf: gwneuthur (gwneud) — to do, make; 1 sg. present/future 'I will do', soft-mutated after a (mi a wnaf hynny) · also 'I will see to it, bring it about that' (mi a wnaf na chaffo ef uiui uyth 'I will see that he never gets me'); auxiliary (Y gymryt a wnaf 'I will take it')
__broaden__.byd: bot (bod) — to be; used two ways: 3 sg. future 'will be' (uyd elsewhere) and, with y-, the vivid present ual y byd 'as he is' · also 2 sg. imperative 'be!' (byd ditheu a'r got honn genhyt 'you be there with this bag')
__broaden__.uwyaf: mawr (mawr) — big, great; superlative mwyaf 'most', soft-mutated (after pei, as after modern po) (A ffei uwyaf y lladei 'the more he would strike') · also soft after a feminine noun, adjective 'greatest, most' (y wreic uwyaf a garaf 'the woman I love most', mwyaf)
__broaden__.genthi: gan — conjugated preposition 'from her' (3 sg. f.) (genthi hi 'from her') · also 'with her' (kyscu genthi 'to sleep with her')
__broaden__.dyro: rodi (rhoi) — to give; negative imperative 'do not give!' (na dyro 'do not give') · also the positive imperative 'give!' (dyro ui idaw 'give me to him', Dyro di ui idaw ef 'you give me to him')
__broaden__.ui: ui (fi) — me; object pronoun after an imperative (dygwch ui odyma 'carry me from here') · also, after ny allaf, probably emphatic 'I' (Ny allaf ui arnaf a dywedy di uyth 'I cannot (act) against what you ever say'); the construction is uncertain
__broaden__.hynn: hynn (hyn) — 'this'; demonstrative, substantive use in ual hynn 'like this, thus' · also adjective 'this' after its noun (seith cantref hynn 'these seven cantrefs')
__broaden__.ouyn: ofyn (ofn) — fear; noun m., u for the v-sound (nyt oes arnaf i ouyn 'I have no fear', literally 'there is no fear on me') · also 3 sg. present of gouyn (gofyn) 'asks', with g lost by soft mutation after a (ef a ouyn yt 'he will ask you'); a different word from ofyn 'fear'
__broaden__.tra: tra (tra) — while; conjunction (tra deweis wrthyt ti 'while I kept silent') · also (2) 'very', before an adjective with spirant mutation (tra chyuoethauc 'very mighty'); (3) 'while' with the verb sometimes soft-mutated (tra barhaud)
__broaden__.yny: yny (hyd oni) — until; so that; conjunction, with a vivid present (yny hyllt, yny dyrr, yny uyd) or the subjunctive for a future goal (yny delych) · also in Ac ar yny llyma, a slip for ar hynny 'thereupon' (the h- lost; ar yny llyma y teulu 'and thereupon, behold the household')
__broaden__.wyr: gwyr (gwŷr) — men; noun pl., soft-mutated after yn (yn wyr ymi 'as men to me') · also soft after o 'of' (o wyr 'of men') and in address (A wyr 'O men') · also soft after y 'to' (y wyr Dyuet 'to the men of Dyfed') and y 'his' (y wyr 'his men')
__broaden__.neb: neb (neb) — anyone; pronoun, used with a positive sense in relative/superlative clauses (o'r a welsei neb 'that anyone had seen') · also 'anyone' under a negative = 'no one' (ny thykya y neb ymlit 'it avails no one to pursue') · also in y neb a 'the one who/to whom' (y neb a dylyer y kymryt y ganthaw 'the one from whom one ought to take it')
__broaden__.ganthaw: gan — conjugated preposition 'with him' (y bu digrif ganthaw 'it was pleasant with him') · also in y ganthaw 'from him' (kymer gedernit y ganthaw 'take a pledge from him')
__broaden__.ymgueiraw: ymgyweiraw — to make oneself ready, settle oneself; reflexive verbal noun, ym- + kyweiraw 'prepare, set in order', written ymgueiraw (ymgueiraw yn y gyfrwy 'settling himself in his saddle') · also ymgueiraw ar 'to equip oneself with, get together' (ymgueiraw ar y ganuet marchauc 'to get ready with his hundred horsemen'); the sense with ar is uncertain
__broaden__.llad: llad (lladd) — to kill; verbal noun, base form (y'm llad i 'to kill me') · also llad glwm 'to tie a knot' (idiomatic, literally 'strike a knot'): llad glwm ar garryeu y got 'to tie a knot on the straps of the bag'
